implication: Material acquisitions of listed company equity require Regulation 30 disclosure and may trigger open offer/takeover code thresholds depending on post-acquisition stake; transactional counsel must review shareholding caps and competition law (CCI Schedule-I carve-outs).

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Regulation 30
framework.note: Material acquisitions must be disclosed immediately; defines 'material' by reference to turnover and net profit thresholds.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Section 4
framework.note: Acquisition of 25% or more of equity (or voting rights) triggers mandatory open offer; acquisitions of 5–25% require disclosure within 2 days.
Acquisitions meeting Schedule-I thresholds (asset value >₹1,000 cr or combined turnover >₹4,000 cr) require CCI approval; exemptions exist for acquisitions of listed companies below 25%.
Shareholder approval or board approval may be required depending on the acquirer's memorandum and articles and the nature of consideration (cash vs. equity).

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 – Section 47(vi) & Schedule VI
framework.note: If share acquisition is structured as a slump sale or involves consideration in equity shares, tax neutrality provisions may apply; transfer of shares may attract TCS under Section 194LA.
If consideration exceeds ₹50 lakh in cash, KYC and beneficial ownership verification mandatory; source of funds documentation required.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) – Schedule I
framework.note: If acquirer or target is a resident individual, HUF, or non-resident, FDI/ODI reporting to RBI Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) or ECB rules may apply.

The filing does not specify the quantum of shares, consideration, or whether the acquisition triggers mandatory open offer obligations under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Takeover Regulations, 2011. GMR Power and Urban Infra Limited is a subsidiary or associate entity within the GMR Airports infrastructure group. The absence of published detailed terms suggests either a pre-announcement of a later formal disclosure or reliance on exemptions.
